proposal.diagnosis: The issue lies in the handling of comment tokens. When a semicolon ';' is encountered, it should be treated as the start of a comment and all subsequent characters until the end of the line should be ignored. However, the current implementation incorrectly processes these characters as separate tokens instead of treating them as part of the comment which should not generate any valid token.

causal_chain: The function `get_token` in lines 183-261 reads characters and transitions states based on DFA rules. When a semicolon is read, it enters state 30 (line 254) which calls `error_or_eof_case`. This function incorrectly processes the semicolon as an error token instead of recognizing it as the start of a comment.
The test cases show that after a semicolon, subsequent tokens are being processed and outputted as errors or valid tokens when they should be ignored entirely.
mr_refs: MR2: Deleting content after ';' in input lines doesn't change token counts but the actual output shows additional error tokens.
MR3: Adding ';' at start of lines converts them to comments, which should not produce any valid tokens. However, the test output still includes tokens from those lines.
testcase_refs: source_s5_mr2: Input with ';if i ` ;nd5 ;YfI8' produces multiple error tokens after each ';'.
followup_s4_mr4: Multiple ';' in input produce multiple error tokens instead of being ignored as comments.

proposal.uncertainty: There are multiple plausible ways to fix the comment handling, but all involve modifying how state 30 in get_token handles semicolons and subsequent characters. The exact implementation may vary but must ensure that no tokens are generated for the rest of the line after a semicolon is encountered.
proposal.assumption: The comment handling should skip all characters until end of line or EOF without generating any token.

edits.rationale: Modify the case 30 to properly handle comments by skipping remaining characters in the line and not returning any token.
edits.replacement: case 30 : return(error_or_eof_case(tstream_ptr,token_ptr,cu_state,token_str,token_ind,ch)); // Fix: Add code to skip until end of line or EOF here

proposal.expected_effect: When a semicolon is encountered, the function will properly skip all remaining characters in the current line and not generate any tokens for them.
preservation_constraints: The rest of the token processing logic should remain unchanged except for comment handling.
proposal.repair_intent: Properly handle comments by skipping until end of line or EOF without generating tokens.
